Hi, I’m Ruiyuan Bai, an HCI researcher pursuing a Master of Fine Arts in Human-Computer Interaction at City University of Hong Kong, advised by Prof. Shengdong Zhao in the Synteraction Lab. I previously earned a BSc (Hons) in Financial Technology & Artificial Intelligence (Computing) at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Studying across mainland China, the United States, and Hong Kong sparked my interest in culture and learning.

I’m applying to master’s programs in education, with a longer-term goal of a PhD in educational technology. I want to build games and interactive stories that help adults explore public and cultural issues beyond formal education.

My research asks how interfaces help people understand information—from audio learning on the go (GlanceMap ↗) to learning and applying traditional Chinese color knowledge (ColoGene ↗, CHI 2026 Poster). I combine prototyping, interviews and experiments. Other published and accepted work includes (PersonaMail ↗, IUI 2026 Companion), (Ambulance Rush! ↗, Australian Journalism Review, 2025), and (Beyond the Gaze ↗, ACM Multimedia Asia 2026, co-first author).

I also make games about young people’s pressures in China (Taste of Connection ↗), overlooked women’s history (Her Sound Re-sound ↗), and animal welfare (Our World ↗), inviting people to consider perspectives they might otherwise miss. Outside work, I love traveling and spending time with my two dogs .
